name: Littlestone Dimension of Half-intervals
details: Exact for the catalogue convention of n nonempty initial segments; the value is zero at n=1. Balanced splits attain the leaf-counting upper bound.
proof: A balanced binary-search tree on the ordered endpoints is shattered: at a queried coordinate, the target initial segment lies on exactly one side of that coordinate, and each branch retains an interval of feasible endpoints.  This gives depth $\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$.  Conversely, a depth-$d$ shattered Littlestone tree has $2^d$ leaves realized by distinct concepts, while the class has only $n$ initial segments.  Hence $d\le\log_2 n$ and the value is logarithmic.
